title: Microstructure–Property Relationships for Zirconia and Titania PVD Coatings on AISI 430 Steel: A Comparative Study of Microtribological Behaviour
content: Oxide coatings, including titanium dioxide and zirconium dioxide, are widely used to protect metals and polymers in industrial, architectural, environmental, aerospace, and biomedical applications. This study compares the surface topography, microstructure, and phase composition of reactive PVD ZrO₂ and TiO₂ coatings and correlates these with their microtribological properties. Hardness and wear/friction behaviour were analysed using nanoindentation, scratch tests, and dry microtribological sliding tests on an indentation tester equipped with a precision rotational stage. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis, white light interferometry (WLI), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) show the peculiarities in the microstructure and phase composition of both nanocrystalline coatings (with grain sizes of ~26 nm and ~11 nm for ZrO₂ and TiO2, respectively). Despite the slightly lower hardness of ZrO₂ (12.57 GPa) in comparison with that of TiO2 (13.88 GPa), the volumetric wear rate is on the order of magnitude lower for the zirconia coating (1.5×105 μm3/m) than that of the titanium dioxide coating (2.2×106 μm3/m). This finding correlates well with the wear track morphology observed by interference profilometry and SEM. Wear mechanisms are discussed in relation to the phase compositions of the studied coatings. As observed, both coatings underwent stress-induced tetragonal to monoclinic phase transformations due to a high enough Hertzian contact pressure (6.6–6.7 GPa) applied at indentation and wear tests. However, the TRIP effect related to the phase transformation in the ZrO2 coating seems to be beneficial for wear resistance enhancement owing to acquired localised ductility and clamping down on crack propagation, while the increased phase misfit and microstresses accumulated in the TiO2 coating resulted in its early brittle fracture and further abrasive wear.
